column1: # Every operation the shipped `pro` surface loses to a name collision.
# Columns: resource <TAB> the name it lost <TAB> method <TAB> path
# Pinned by TestTheDroppedOperationSetIsPinned, because the loss is reported as a
# warning on stderr and exit 0 — so a new one is a line in `make generate`'s
# output that nobody reads, and seven writes went missing under exactly that.
# Two rows are worth reading before adding a third.
# deliberate: resourceGetDetailPathOverrides puts the detail endpoint and
# /v4/computers-inventory/{id} behind one `get`, the first serving the call and
# the second serving `--section`, so the operation is dropped and its path is
# real defect and a pre-existing one: the collection-level PUT keeps `update`,
# so `update` replaces the whole list rather than one field. Both operations
# address the resource's own root, so deciding between them is a naming judgement
# (`update <id>` against a bulk `update-all`) rather than the precedence rule
# qualifyDuplicateVerbsOutsideTheRoot applies, and it is not this change.
# What the test refuses outright is a root operation losing its name to a
# *sub-path's*, since a resource's plain verbs are its root's. Every other row
# here is a collision between two sub-paths.
